This is the first hadith of the collection “Sahih al-Bukhari” — the most authentic collection of hadith.

It was narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), the second rightly guided caliph.

Meaning: every deed of a person is judged by its intention. The same outward act — work, help, even moving for university — can be rewarded or be an empty deed depending on what is in the heart: for the sake of Allah or for people's praise.

Imam an-Nawawi placed this hadith first in his “Forty Hadith” and called it a third of Islam: intention accompanies every action.
